newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwandan refugees flee Tanzanian camps.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees flee Tanzanian camps.

text.p: Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees abandoned two entire camps in Tanzania's Karagwe region on Sunday, aid workers said.
The refugees fled from Kagenyi and Rubwera camps which had held about 41,000 Rwandans and are part of a chain of five camps in northwestern Tanzania with a total of 110,000 refugees.
"These two camps appear to be empty now," Bradley Guerrant of the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said in Ngara.

Aid workers said hardline Hutu groups may have organised the mass exodus in response to an order by the Tanzanian government to all the 542,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in Tanzania to return to Rwanda by the end of this month.
Many Hutus refuse to go back to Rwanda, now controlled by a Tutsi-led army, for fear of being accused of taking part in the mass slaughter of one million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus in 1994.
Guerrant said they had little information about the direction the refugees were taking in their flight from Kagenyi and Rubwera, but they did not appear to be heading for the Rwanda border.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has supported the Tanzanian government's demand that the refugees go back, a position that was condemned by the human rights group Amnesty International as effectively sanctioning forced repatriation.
The UNHCR says 562,000 Rwandan Hutus had returned to Rwanda from wartorn eastern Zaire by last Wednesday, an exodus that prompted Tanzania to rid itself of its unwanted guests.
Tanzanian regional authorities, in an effort to encourage the refugees to return home, have banned economic activity and further building work in the camps in Karagwe region.
Refugee workers said 4,667 Rwandan Hutus had registered to return to Rwanda from Ngara camp. It was hoped this would be the beginning of a larger exodus.
